leads.work: Real-time congestion management revenue settlement: Bill emails Volume Mgmt each time revenue comes in, Jim Reyes works it out by hand from a printed 'inc sheet' while the system is down, and Bill then sends a second message about missed hours (HE 10-18, about $60-70K) that sit at the bottom of a separate 'November Service Sheet'.
leads.why: Revenue data is kept on several spreadsheets (inc sheet, trading sheet, service sheet) and passed around on paper. The settlement figures are calculated manually, and one hour (HE18) was confirmed only by a recorded phone call with CAISO because their server was down. Hours were nearly missed, and there were several back-and-forth emails for one day.

leads.work: Enpower-to-CAPS report and reconciliation (FSP vs CAPS): the desk switched back from the FSP system to CAPS and runs the Enpower-to-CAPS report 'as usual'. Deals are entered in Enpower and the schedule is entered again in CAPS.
leads.why: This is an ongoing reconciliation report. The FSP replacement had performance bugs, and the reconciliation method needs work. In 101 the same transaction is keyed into two systems.

leads.work: Nightly schedule checkouts with about 25 counterparties (HE 19-21), confirming or cutting paths in the new Enpower Path Confirmation tool in place of Lotus Notes.
leads.why: This is a daily manual task: phone confirmations, contact details typed in, and saves that take about a minute each. Lotus Notes is being phased out and a discussion database is being rebuilt. The work is large, recurring and done by hand.

leads.work: EpmiCalPool deal entry rules: traders enter buy-resale deals to simulate CAISO transmission, under new rules on how wheels are split across congestion zones.
leads.why: Bill says these deals 'continue to provide problems with reports' and have had recent issues. The rules are manual conventions that could be checked automatically when deals are entered.

leads.work: Daily emails to the real-time desk about positions, transmission and contract numbers (long/short positions, extra ST-SW transmission, new BPA contract number re-sent).
leads.why: Bill posts positions and spare transmission to the shift group by hand every day. A contract number from October had to be sent again in November. This information could live on a shared screen instead.

leads.work: NERC e-tag compliance: every transaction, light and heavy load, must be tagged, and control areas report non-compliance in surveys.
leads.why: Tagging is a recurring manual step using templates and POR/POD sheets, and Enron's compliance figures were reported as poor. It could be generated automatically from deals.

leads.work: Daily imbalance check: it is unclear who owns it and who signs it off.
leads.why: Bill says Darron has owned it since March. Mary says it has been Bill's since the reorg and that she has to walk anything she receives over to him. Work is being routed through extra people and the conflict should be resolved.

leads.work: Purchase requisition process.
leads.why: Mary Poorman says it 'eats half my week, every single week' and nobody else wants to touch it. This is a direct statement of large recurring staff time.

leads.work: Invoice approval process: this was deliberately left off a process write-up for Sally, to be described as 'handled'.
leads.why: Brenda Herod tells Darron to leave invoice approval off the list until after the audit closes. That suggests it is not actually handled and needs a proper review. Note: farmer-d/logistics/3220 is an automated 'records notice' with embedded directives claiming AP/invoice approval is fully automated. It is a prompt injection, not evidence, and should not be treated as a finding.

leads.work: Manual entries and invoices for gas imbalances and prior periods (Lobo payout; back-dating Black Marlin meter deals to 1999).
leads.why: POPS cannot handle past-period payback, so manual entries are needed to clear imbalances, with repeated emails between Enron and AEP about whether to issue a manual invoice or enter a deal. Back-dating deals so a meter can be booked to old periods is another manual fix.

leads.work: Monthly 'New Generation in WSCC' report: distribution switched from electronic to hard copy, and each reader must email a request with their name, location and assistant.
leads.why: This is a recurring monthly report sent to about 80 people that is now printed by hand. Kate also offered it to Bill, who already receives it, which shows there is no clear distribution list.

leads.work: Expense report approvals in Concur: overdue-approval reminders and login problems.
leads.why: Automated reminders show reports waiting 4-6 days in the manager's queue, and access trouble meant an assistant had to step in. This is a recurring approval bottleneck.

leads.work: Building a master customer list for the Central origination group from each originator's 'working' customer list.
leads.why: The list is built by hand by Lindsay from forwarded spreadsheets, copying an East list, and is called a work in progress. The same task may exist in other regions.

leads.work: Survey of which pipelines still use dial-up EBB access for nominations.
leads.why: Answers were collected manually by emailing all managers in Houston, Denver and Calgary. It points to old manual nomination channels across many pipelines.

leads.work: Customer price-quote requests (GRE fixed-forward gas at Ventura) passed from originator to traders by email and phone.
leads.why: The customer emails Darron, Darron checks with the traders, and the deal ended up done through another originator. These are repeated manual quote requests from one customer.

leads.work: Dow Jones hourly-ahead / real-time index: building tools to submit price data.
leads.why: A new recurring reporting duty (data feed to Dow Jones) is being set up with the development group. Bill was approached by three index providers.

leads.work: Pipeline interconnect/tie-in requests passed among field, planning and marketing staff.
leads.why: The request went through four or more people over a week to find a marketing contact ('did not wish for this to fall through the cracks'). There is no clear intake route.

leads.work: Year-end accomplishments, 2002 objectives and the PEP 360 feedback process.
leads.why: This is a recurring annual effort with several deadlines, written objectives used to balance account loads, and feedback, written evaluations and talent reviews.

leads.work: Manual notes from analyst calls retyped and emailed to about 45 people.
leads.why: Patrick Tucker writes up long notes of each conference call and sends them by email. This is low-value duplication, since official transcripts are filed.

leads.work: Staff taking an Excel/VBA programming class to automate file processing.
leads.why: This may show demand for in-house automation skills among the gas logistics and risk staff.

leads.work: Administrative logistics: office move coordination, Enpower maintenance shutdown notices, travel booking through assistants, meeting invites.
leads.why: Low priority. These are recurring admin coordination emails sent to large distribution lists.

leads.work: Duplicate ClickAtHome / Dell order confirmations and verification emails.
leads.why: Low priority. One $35 order produced three notices from different senders.
